messages.content:
The record:
Write the postmortem for the incident below.

Alert: CachedSpendTotalsAreStale on io-shop
What the alert said [AL1]: 90 {A1} of 240 {A2} cached spend figures disagree with the purchases behind them. The purchases are correct and the cached copies are behind: the widest gap is 89.29 {A3}, the most any one figure is missing is 1 {A4} purchase, and the oldest purchase none of them account for was recorded at 2026-11-10T23:13:00Z {A5}, which is when the copies stopped keeping up, and they were being served from 2026-11-11T02:07:30Z {A6}. Discarding the entries listed will send those pages back to the purchase ledger, which never moved. The list is what disagreed when this check ran: nothing is putting the copies right, so a figure goes stale as soon as its shopper buys again and a later check will name more.
Alert raised: 2026-11-11T02:12:54Z {alert_raised}
Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one. An alert rule fires; a person is paged. Argus first posted about the incident in Slack at 2026-11-11T02:12:58Z {first_told}, and the document says so already: leave that post out, and do not say that no person was told. That nobody was paged is a finding of its own.
The alert rule fires as soon as its condition holds. The alert came 5 minutes 24 seconds {alerted_after_the_onset} after the onset.
Broken from 2026-11-11T02:07:30Z {began} (the onset). The service was not back to normal by 2026-11-11T02:13:25Z {argus_stopped}, so it was broken for at least 5 minutes 55 seconds {duration} - a lower bound, not a measurement, and every impact figure below is bounded the same way.
Argus held the incident for 30 seconds {held}, until 2026-11-11T02:13:25Z {argus_stopped}. That is not how long the fault lasted, nor how long Argus went on working - leave it out of your answer.
Error rate: not measured by the metrics - the metrics for the incident could not be read.
Customer loss: none so far - the shop's takings over the incident fell short of the same hours whole weeks earlier by no more than those hours vary on their own, if at all; a lower bound, counted with the service not seen back to normal.

What Argus did, in order:
  - [T1] 2026-11-11T02:12:55Z {T1.1} Argus: Received CachedSpendTotalsAreStale on io-shop
  - [T2] 2026-11-11T02:13:03Z {T2.1} Argus: Moved the incident to INVESTIGATING - a worker took the incident up
  - [T3] 2026-11-11T02:13:03Z {T3.1} Argus: Called in the Investigator Agent
  - [T4] 2026-11-11T02:13:11Z {T4.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's per-minute metrics, anchored on 02:12:54 {T4.2}
  - [T5] 2026-11-11T02:13:13Z {T5.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 0 {T5.2} minutes of metrics
  - [T6] 2026-11-11T02:13:13Z {T6.1} Investigator Agent: Placed the start of the incident at 02:07 {T6.2}
  - [T7] 2026-11-11T02:13:13Z {T7.1} Investigator Agent: Recorded where the 3 {T7.2} replicas run - all on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB
  - [T8] 2026-11-11T02:13:14Z {T8.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 {T8.2} day 5 {T8.3} minutes 24 {T8.4} seconds before Nov 11 02:12:54 {T8.5}
  - [T9] 2026-11-11T02:13:14Z {T9.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 0 {T9.2} production changes
  - [T10] 2026-11-11T02:13:15Z {T10.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's log lines, the 35 {T10.2} minutes 24 {T10.3} seconds before 02:12:54 {T10.4}
  - [T11] 2026-11-11T02:13:15Z {T11.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 0 {T11.2} log lines
  - [T12] 2026-11-11T02:13:15Z {T12.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's log lines, the 3 {T12.2} hours before Nov 11 02:12:31 {T12.3}
  - [T13] 2026-11-11T02:13:16Z {T13.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 0 {T13.2} log lines
  - [T14] 2026-11-11T02:13:16Z {T14.1} Investigator Agent: Read the service register - the service calls io-pricing (internal, owned by checkout-platform), io-summary-cache (internal, owned by checkout-platform), io-pay (third-party, owned by IO Payments Ltd)
  - [T15] 2026-11-11T02:13:17Z {T15.1} Investigator Agent: Formed 2 {T15.2} candidate causes, best first: C1, C2
  - [T16] 2026-11-11T02:13:17Z {T16.1} Investigator Agent: Read every channel available
  - [T17] 2026-11-11T02:13:17Z {T17.1} Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 0 {T17.2} flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 {T17.3} hour before 02:13:17 {T17.4}
  - [T18] 2026-11-11T02:13:22Z {T18.1} Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATING to act on a candidate
  - [T19] 2026-11-11T02:13:22Z {T19.1} Argus: Called in the Mitigation Agent
  - [T20] 2026-11-11T02:13:23Z {T20.1} Mitigation Agent: Discarded the stale cached figures of io-shop for C1
  - [T21] 2026-11-11T02:13:25Z {T21.1} Mitigation Agent: Judged the action CONFIRMED
  - [T22] 2026-11-11T02:13:25Z {T22.1} Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATED - discarded [90 {T22.2}] of [io-shop]'s stale cached figures and the store reported what it removed, which is the whole of what was wrong
  - [T23] 2026-11-11T02:15:02Z {T23.1} Code-Fix Agent: Proposed a fix as a draft pull request - https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/528

Changes to production it read:
  - Deploys read, none came back; flags read, none came back.

Log lines it read, one per message:
  - Read; none came back.

Candidates it considered, in the Investigator's words - name them by their labels, but cite none; what they claim is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [C1, also C2] Candidates blaming the same move of io-summary-cache, each reading it as a different kind of failure - different accounts of what it did, not one cause counted twice - each in its own words:
      C1: The cached spend totals (io-summary-cache) stopped keeping up with the purchase ledger from 2026-11-10T23:13:00Z {C1.1} and began being served stale at 2026-11-11T02:07:30Z {C1.2}. The ledger is correct and only the derived copy is behind. No deploy, flag or placement change was recorded. [state-divergence, confidence 0.7 {C1.3}, confirmed]
      C2: The internal io-summary-cache service, owned by checkout-platform, failed to apply updates and so served stale totals. [internal-dependency-failure, confidence 0.15 {C1.4}, confirmed, as tested for C1]

Actions it took:
  - [M1] Discarded the stale cached figures of io-shop for [C1] - confirmed, nothing to put back

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix, and what it claims is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [F1] The fault: in src/io_shop/account_page.py, `_the_figure_for` returned `found.amount_cents` for any entry `cached_summary` handed back. It never compared the entry with the account it was rendering. An entry that stopped being updated went on being served as long as the cache could be reached, so the page had no defence against a cache that fell behind the ledger. Nothing was deployed and no flag changed: the cache's feed just stopped keeping up, and every page read whatever the cache still held.
      
      The data to catch this was already there. A `SummaryEntry` (src/io_shop/summary_cache.py) holds `items_counted`, the number of purchases the figure was worked out over. The page already has `account.purchases` loaded, and src/io_shop/cache_reconciliation.py uses that same comparison (`len(account.purchases) - entry.items_counted`) to report stale entries. The page now runs the check before serving: an entry is used only when `items_counted == len(account.purchases)`. Anything else is treated like a miss, so the page works the figure out from the purchases (the same fallback it already uses for a miss or an unreachable cache), reports `served_from_cache=False`, and the share of recomputed pages shows the drift. The cache stays optional, `CacheUnreachable` handling is unchanged, and pages without a cache configured are untouched.
      
      Tests (tests/io_shop/test_account_page.py): `a_cache_holding` now takes the purchase count. The existing cached-figure test builds an entry that matches the account's two purchases. Before, it used a hard-coded count of 8 {F1.1}, which only passed because the count was never checked. A new test builds an entry counting one purchase for an account with two. It asserts the page shows the computed figure (2000 {F1.2}), not the cached one, and reports `served_from_cache` as False. Against the current code that test would get 999 {F1.3} and True.
      
      Limit: this catches entries that missed purchases or count extra ones. It would not catch an entry with the right count but a wrong amount. That isn't the stale-copy pattern the investigation describes.
  - Say what the files Code-Fix read do, with the conditions it gives - a default as a default, never as all it does - and no wider: 'nothing in the files it read', never 'nothing in the code'.

Action items the record already holds:
  - AI-1 (mitigate, done): Discarded the stale cached figures of io-shop
  - AI-2 (mitigate, open): Review and merge the proposed fix
PR #528 is a draft Argus opened for a person to review and merge. The record holds nothing about it after that: do not say it was reviewed, approved or merged, or that it was not - nor that the record holds nothing, which the document says itself. Nothing ran its test or its fix: say what it proposes, not that it corrects anything.

Cite evidence in causal_chain by its label. In a contributing factor's addressed_by, name the record's own action items that answer it, by their number; an item you propose names the factors it answers in its answers, by their labels.

Call submit_postmortem with your answer.

The document, by field:
root_cause: The cached spend entries in io-summary-cache stopped taking in new purchases from {A5}, so they fell behind the purchase ledger, which stayed correct. The evidence read does not show why the updates stopped.
cause_in_plain_words: The shop keeps saved copies of each shopper's running spend total, and these copies stopped being updated with new purchases for a reason the record does not show; account pages kept showing the out-of-date copies, likely because a page did not check a copy against the shopper's purchases before showing it.
still_at_risk: Cached spend figures that were not on the discarded list, and any that went stale later, could keep showing shoppers totals that leave out their latest purchases, and more would go stale each time a shopper bought again.
symptom: Account pages showed shoppers spend totals missing their latest purchases
causal_chain 1: Shoppers' account pages showed spend totals that left out purchases they had made. The purchases themselves were recorded correctly. (cites AL1)
causal_chain 2: The pages were serving cached copies of the spend figures from io-summary-cache that had fallen behind the purchase ledger, while the ledger itself stayed correct. These stale cached copies were the whole of what was wrong. (cites AL1; T22, under "What Argus did, in order")
causal_chain 3: The cached copies stopped taking in new purchases from {A5}. The oldest purchase that no stale figure counted was recorded then. What stopped the updates is not shown: the Investigator Agent got back no metrics and no log lines for the service. (cites AL1; T5, under "What Argus did, in order"; T11, under "What Argus did, in order"; T13, under "What Argus did, in order")
contributing_factors 1: Code-Fix read src/io_shop/account_page.py, and nothing ran that reading. In it, the account page's `_the_figure_for` serves any entry the cache returns without comparing the entry's purchase count with the purchases the page has already loaded for that account. So a stale entry kept being served for as long as the cache could be reached.
contributing_factors 1 had_it_been_otherwise: Pages would have treated an entry with a mismatched purchase count as a miss and worked the figure out from the purchases, so shoppers would not have been shown stale totals even with the cache's updates stopped.
contributing_factors 2: Nothing was seen watching whether io-summary-cache's updates kept up with the purchase ledger. The copies stopped keeping up at {A5}, and the only thing that found it was the stale-figure check, once stale figures were being served.
contributing_factors 2 had_it_been_otherwise: The stopped updates could have been caught and dealt with before any stale figure reached a shopper.
contributing_factors 3: The CachedSpendTotalsAreStale alert was not linked to an on-call incident, so nobody was paged.
contributing_factors 3 had_it_been_otherwise: A person could have taken up the stopped cache updates, which the discarding of entries did not touch, and so shortened how long figures kept going stale.
contributing_factors 4: No per-minute metrics and no log lines came back for the service when the Investigator Agent asked for them.
contributing_factors 4 had_it_been_otherwise: The investigation could have seen what stopped the cache's updates and put it right, rather than only clearing the entries that were stale at that moment.
action_items 1: Restore io-summary-cache's updates so cached spend figures take in new purchases again.
action_items 2: Until the cache's updates are restored, re-run the stale-figure check and discard the entries it names.
action_items 3: Find out what stopped io-summary-cache from taking in new purchases from {A5}, including any change made to io-summary-cache itself.
action_items 4: Add an alert that fires when io-summary-cache's updates fall behind the purchase ledger, whether or not stale entries are being served yet.
action_items 5: Route CachedSpendTotalsAreStale to on-call paging so that a person is paged when it fires.
action_items 6: Make io-shop's per-minute metrics readable to the Investigator Agent.
action_items 7: Make io-shop's log lines readable to the Investigator Agent, or find out why none came back for the hours before the alert.
went_well 1: The alert named each stale entry and pointed to a safe fallback: the purchase ledger, which never moved. That made it clear what to discard.
went_wrong 1: The mitigation discarded only the entries that disagreed when the alert's check ran. Nothing seen restarted the cache's updates, so the copies were left free to go stale again.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {T5.1} or {duration}, are figures code writes in from the row they name. They are not judged.
  - Action items propose what to do; they make no claim about the record.
  - Whether something went well, went wrong or was lucky is a judgement. Only a fact it states is judged.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
